title: How to Learn from What a Human Would Avoid? Intervention-Aware World Models with Real-World RL for Dexterous Manipulation
title_zh: 如何学习人类会避开的状态：面向灵巧操作真实强化学习的干预感知世界模型
abstract: Multi-fingered dexterous manipulation remains challenging for real-world reinforcement learning because of high-dimensional actions and costly hardware failures. Human-in-the-loop RL lets operators intervene before failures, but often treats interventions only as reactive corrections. WHIRL transforms binary interventions into forward-predictive signals for proactive risk avoidance. Its latent world model has dynamics, reward, termination, and intervention-probability heads; the latter predicts future human takeover and supplies actor-side risk shaping that discourages intervention-prone states. On a 16-DoF LEAP Hand, predictive risk shaping reaches 96.7% success on complex grasping and reduces step-weighted intervention burden by up to 84%.
